options: Seeds require air, water and food to germinate.

subject: Science

options: The potato in beaker J took a shorter time to digest because it has a smaller exposed surface area.
The potato in beaker J took a shorter time to digest because it has a larger exposed surface area.
The potato in beaker K took a shorter time to digest because it has a smaller exposed surface area.
The potato in beaker K took a shorter time to digest because it has a larger exposed surface area.
answer: The potato in beaker J took a shorter time to digest because it has a larger exposed surface area.

subject: Science
text:
Kate studied the effect of temperature on the growth of bacteria H (5 units at the start each time). At the end: 30 °C — 130; 35 °C — 265; 40 °C — 115; 45 °C — 60. Which statements are correct?
A: Bacteria H grows the most at 35 °C.
B: Bacteria H grows the least at 45 °C.
C: As temperature increases, bacteria H grows faster.

subject: Science
text:
Elroy counted Insect G in his garden at different times of the day:
8.00 am — Tue 7, Wed 10, Thu 6
1.00 pm — Tue 19, Wed 16, Thu 17
6.00 pm — Tue 8, Wed 7, Thu 9
Which is the best conclusion that can be made from the table?
options: Insect G are most active during the afternoon.
Insect G prefer a cool surrounding to a warm surrounding.
The temperature at Elroy's garden on Thursday was the highest.
The time of the day does not affect the number of Insect G observed at Elroy's garden.
answer: Insect G are most active during the afternoon.

subject: Science
text:

B: Count the number of Insect G at two other gardens in the area.
C: Count the number of Insect G at his garden for another 2 days.
D: Count the number of Insect G at his garden at 10 am and 3 pm as well.

subject: Science
text: A block of ice was placed in an empty paper cup and left in the class. Some water formed around the ice. What will happen after some time?
options: The temperature of the block of ice increases.
The temperature of the block of ice decreases.
The temperature of the water around the block of ice is 0 °C.
The temperature of the water around the block of ice is less than 0 °C.
answer: The temperature of the water around the block of ice is 0 °C.

subject: Science
text: Mary set up an experiment with a measuring cylinder of water to find out whether the length of an object will affect its volume. Which of the following should Mary keep the same to ensure a fair test?
options: volume of water before adding the object
final volume of water in the measuring cylinder
answer: volume of water before adding the object

subject: Science
text: The properties of substance W: at 42 °C it takes the shape of its container but cannot be compressed; at 88 °C it takes the shape of its container and can be compressed. Which statement is possible about substance W?
options: W is in the solid state at 58 °C.
W is in the gaseous state at 74 °C.
answer: W is in the gaseous state at 74 °C.

subject: Science
text:
Wilma tested four ropes of the same length and thickness, made of different materials:
P: 1 kg did not break, 3 kg did not break, 5 kg broke
Q: 1 kg did not break, 3 kg did not break, 5 kg did not break
R: 1 kg broke, 3 kg broke, 5 kg broke
S: 1 kg did not break, 3 kg broke, 5 kg broke
Arrangement A: rope P holds a 1 kg load with rope S and a 2 kg load hanging below. Arrangement B: rope Q holds a 2 kg load with rope R and a 3 kg load below. Arrangement C: rope P holds a 3 kg load with rope R and a 1 kg load below. Which arrangements are possible (no rope breaks)?

subject: Science
text:
James moved four bar magnets of different sizes, E, F, G and H, towards some pins and recorded the furthest distance, d, at which each magnet attracted some pins: E 6 cm, F 7 cm, G 4 cm, H 5 cm (H is the largest magnet). What can James infer?
A: Only magnet H can attract pins 5 cm away.
B: Magnet F is stronger than magnet E.
C: The greater the size of the magnet, the stronger the magnet.
D: Magnet H can attract more pins than magnet G when the pins are placed the same distance away from them.

subject: Science
text: Jack labelled three bars, A (ends E, F), B (ends G, H) and C (ends J, K). He brought the ends together: E and H repelled; E and G attracted; G and J attracted; H and J attracted. Which conclusion is NOT correct?
options: Bar A will attract bar C.
Bars A and B are magnets.
Bars A, B and C are magnets.
Bar C is made of a magnetic material.
answer: Bars A, B and C are magnets.

subject: Science
text:
A factory makes 6 materials. P, Q and T do not allow light to pass through; R, S and U allow most light to pass through. Five children stand behind walls made of these materials, in this order: Vani | U, S | Jill | R | Kim | P | Ben | Q, U | Alan | T. Which statements are correct?
A: Alan can see Ben.
B: Kim can see Vani.
C: Vani cannot see Ben.
D: Jill cannot see Kim.

subject: Science
text: A train track is made of long steel bars with small gaps between them. The gaps were smaller on a hot day. What is the reason for leaving gaps between the steel bars?
options: To reduce the weight on the track.
To make the track easier to install.
To prevent the track from getting rusty.
To allow the track to expand without causing damage.
answer: To allow the track to expand without causing damage.

subject: Science
text: The diagrams show the temperature of water before and after cooling. By how much did the temperature of the water drop after cooling?

subject: Science
text: An ice cube was trapped by a wire mesh at the bottom of a tilted glass tube containing water. The water was heated near the top. After some time, the water near the top started to boil, but the ice cube did not melt. Which statement best explains why the ice cube did not melt?
options: Water is a poor conductor of heat.
Heat was used up to boil the water near the top.
Heat travelled from the lower place to the higher place.
Melting point of ice is higher than the boiling point of water.
answer: Water is a poor conductor of heat.

In which circuit(s) will the changes cause bulb Q to be brighter?

subject: Science
text:
The diagram shows the human digestive system with parts J, K, L and M.
(a) State where, J, K, L or M, (i) digestion ends; (ii) water is absorbed from undigested food.
(b) State what digestion is.
answer: (a) (i) L (ii) M  (b) Digestion is the process where food is broken down into simpler substances by digestive juices and absorbed into the bloodstream in the small intestine.

subject: Science
text:
The diagram shows two flowers from the same plant (with anthers hanging out and large feathery stigmas).
(b) Are the flowers pollinated by wind or by animal?
(c) Explain your answer in part (b).
The second diagram shows fruit G (with fine hair) and fruit H (with stiff hair) from two different types of plants.
(d) Explain how the hair-like part on each fruit helps the plants grow in new places.
(Part of the original question is not included here.)
answer: (b) By wind  (c) Any one: the anthers hang out, exposed to the wind, so the pollen grains are blown away easily; the large feathery stigma is exposed to the wind to catch pollen grains easily.  (d) Fruit G: the fine hair helps the fruit to float in the wind/air longer. Fruit H: the stiff hair clings onto animals' fur when an animal walks past, and the fruit drops further away from the parent plant.
solution: Note: Part (a) (draw an arrow on the diagram) left out — drawing task.

subject: Science
text:
Jerome made flowers with petals of the same size from bright red cards and added different numbers of drops of a sweet-smelling substance to the centre of each. Number of insects visiting the flowers (1st, 2nd, 3rd hour): 5 drops — 8, 6, 1; 10 drops — 9, 10, 5; 15 drops — 10, 12, 8.
(a) What can he conclude about the intensity of the sweet smell of flowers and the number of insects visiting the flowers?
(b) Why is it an advantage for the plant if the flowers are more sweet-smelling?
(c) Suggest two changes to the set-up if Jerome wants to find out how the size of the petals affects the number of insects visiting the flowers.
answer: (a) As the intensity of the sweet smell increases, the number of insects visiting the flowers increases.  (b) More flowers could be pollinated / there is a higher chance of pollination.  (c) (i) Change the petal (coloured) cards to different sizes. (ii) Keep the number of drops of sweet-smelling substance the same.

subject: Science
text:
A, B, C and D are stages in the life cycle of a mosquito.
(a) Name stage D.
(b) Based on the diagram, state a similarity between stages C and D.
Jerry recorded the number of mosquito eggs (out of 40) that hatched in a day at 3 temperatures, three attempts each (graph).
(c) Describe what Jerry could conclude about the effect of changes in temperature on the hatching of mosquito eggs.
answer: (a) Pupa  (b) Both live in water / both breathe through breathing tubes.  (c) As the temperature increases from 22 °C to 28 °C, the number of eggs hatched in a day increases. As the temperature increases from 28 °C to 38 °C, the number of eggs hatched in a day decreases.

subject: Science
text:
Aziz placed a container made of material M, holding liquid X at 20 °C, in a basin of water at 95 °C and recorded the temperature of liquid X. He repeated the experiment with a container made of material N. The graph shows that liquid X in container M reached 70 °C sooner than in container N.
Aziz wanted to bring hot food and cold drinks for a learning journey, keeping the food hot and the drinks cold.
(a) Which material would be more suitable for (i) the hot food container and (ii) the cold drinks container — M or N?
(b) Explain your answers in part (a).
answer: (a) (i) N (ii) N  (b) Evidence: liquid X in container N took a longer time to reach 70 °C. Reason: N is a poorer conductor of heat than M.

subject: Science
text:
Mel wants to find out how the number of coils affects the strength of an electromagnet (iron rod with coils of wire, battery, paper clips). Set-ups X and Y:
Material of rod — X: iron; Y: (i) ____
Length of rod — X: (ii) ____; Y: 20 cm
Number of batteries used — X: (iii) ____; Y: 1
Number of coils of wire around the rod — X: 15; Y: (iv) ____
(a) Fill in the missing information to make sure she conducts a fair experiment.
(b) Suggest another change to the set-up so that the electromagnet could attract the paper clips from a further distance.
answer: (a) (i) iron (ii) 20 cm (iii) 1 (iv) any number other than 15 (less than 15 or more than 15)  (b) Any one: increase the number of coils of wire around the iron rod; add more batteries (connected in series) to the circuit; use batteries of a higher voltage.

subject: Science
text:
(a) State how shadows are formed.
Jenny tested four materials for her puppets by placing each between a torch and a light sensor. Amount of light detected: P 50, Q 300, R 250, S 150 units.
(b) Which material should she choose to make puppets that cast the darkest shadows on the screen? Explain your answer.
(c) Jenny observed that the size of the shadow changed as she moved the puppet to different distances from the light source. What can Jenny do to increase the size of the shadow cast on the screen by the puppet?
answer: (a) Shadows are formed when the path of light is blocked by an opaque object.  (b) P. The least amount of light passes through it.  (c) Move the puppet closer to the light source.

subject: Science
text:
Indra wanted to find out how the mass of substance X affected the volume of air in a syringe connected to a flask containing X. Volume of gas in the syringe (start → end): 30 g of X — 50 → 47 cm³; 40 g — 50 → 43 cm³; 50 g — 50 → 39 cm³.
(a) State how the volume of gas in the syringe changed with the mass of X.
(b) State the property of substance X that allows it to be measured.
Indra placed a flask with a balloon on top in a freezer. At the end of the experiment the balloon had deflated.
(c) Explain the change observed in the balloon at the end of the experiment.
answer: (a) As the mass of X increases, the volume of the gas decreases.  (b) X has mass.  (c) The air inside the flask and balloon loses heat to the surrounding (colder) air, so the air contracts / decreases in volume.

subject: Science
text:
Kyle held a cool metal tray above a kettle of boiling water and collected water in a measuring cylinder over 10 minutes.
(a) Explain how water is collected in the measuring cylinder.
(b) Kyle used a measuring cylinder instead of a beaker to collect the water. Explain how this helps Kyle obtain more accurate results.
answer: (a) The water gained heat from the heat source and boiled to become steam. The steam rises and comes into contact with the cooler underside surface of the metal tray, loses heat and condenses to become water, which drips into the measuring cylinder.  (b) The measuring cylinder has more markings for measuring the same given volume of water.

subject: Science
text:
Barry set up two circuits, W and Z, with identical bulbs A, B, C and D. Circuit W uses more batteries than circuit Z. He measured the brightness of the bulbs in each circuit.
(a) Write a suitable hypothesis for Barry's investigation.
(Part of the original question is not included here.)
answer: If the number of batteries added to the circuit (in series) increases, then the brightness of the bulbs increases.
solution: Note: Parts (b) and (c) (mark switch positions / complete a circuit) left out — drawing tasks.

subject: Science
text:
John tested whether electricity flows through rods X, Y and Z (made of different materials). In his circuit, rods X and Y are connected side by side (in parallel) and rod Z is in series with them. When the switch was closed, the bulb lit up.
(a) John concluded that rods X, Y and Z are definitely conductors of electricity. For each rod, is the statement 'this rod definitely conducts electricity' True, False or Not possible to tell? (i) Rod X (ii) Rod Y (iii) Rod Z
(b) Explain your answers to parts (a)(i) and (ii).
answer: (a) (i) X — Not possible to tell (ii) Y — Not possible to tell (iii) Z — True  (b) Rods X and Y are arranged in parallel, so electric current could flow through either rod X or rod Y.

options: E testes, F ovaries, G style, H stigma
E testes, F ovaries, G ovules, H anther
E ovaries, F testes, G ovules, H anther
E ovaries, F testes, G stigma, H style
answer: E ovaries, F testes, G ovules, H anther

subject: Science
text: Jenny has a plant in her garden that produces brightly-coloured flowers. She removed the petals of one of the flowers. She observed that the flower without petals took a longer time to develop into a fruit compared to the flower with petals. Which one of the following statements about the flower without petals best explains Jenny's observation?
options: The anthers produced lesser pollen grains.
The stigma was unable to catch the pollen grains in the wind.
The pollinators were less attracted to the flower to carry out pollination.
The pollinators were less attracted to the flower to carry out germination.
answer: The pollinators were less attracted to the flower to carry out pollination.

subject: Science
text: Cayden removed the food-carrying tubes from a tree as shown (on the branch below fruit P, where fruit Q grows). After two weeks, she noticed that only fruit P became bigger. Which of the following explains why only fruit P became bigger?
options: Fruit P was able to make more food than fruit Q.
Water taken in by the roots was transported to fruit P only.
Food made by the leaves was transported to fruit P but not fruit Q.
Water-carrying tubes transported more water to fruit Q than to fruit P.
answer: Food made by the leaves was transported to fruit P but not fruit Q.

subject: Science
text: (Same set-up: Cayden removed the food-carrying tubes on one branch of the tree.) Which of the following is a possible observation of the whole plant after a few weeks?
options: The tree continues to grow well.
The roots do not get enough food and shrank.
Fruit Q does not get enough water and dried up.
answer: The tree continues to grow well.

subject: Science
text: Which of the following correctly shows the function of the nose and the lungs?
options: nose: moistens the air; lungs: pump air around the body
nose: has tiny hairs to filter the air; lungs: allow for gaseous exchange
nose: carbon dioxide is removed from the blood; lungs: moisten the air
nose: oxygen is removed from the blood; lungs: allow for gaseous exchange
answer: nose: has tiny hairs to filter the air; lungs: allow for gaseous exchange

subject: Science
text: Which of the following correctly shows the comparison of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the air that we breathe?
options: There is a higher amount of oxygen in exhaled air than in inhaled air.
There is a lower amount of carbon dioxide in inhaled air than in exhaled air.
The amount of oxygen in inhaled and exhaled air remains the same.
The amount of carbon dioxide in inhaled and exhaled air remains the same.
answer: There is a lower amount of carbon dioxide in inhaled air than in exhaled air.

transports waste materials away from different parts of the body for removal

The animal takes 5 weeks to become an adult after the egg is laid.
After the young hatches from the egg, it takes 17 weeks to become an adult.

Switch off the lights when leaving a room.
Choose electrical appliances with less green ticks.

text: Kumar is holding a metal plate in one hand and a wooden plate in the other. He noticed that the metal plate felt cold but not the wooden plate. If both plates were in the same room for the same duration, why did the metal plate feel cold while the wooden plate did not?
options: The temperature of the metal plate is higher than Kumar's hand.

The metal plate gained more heat from Kumar's hand than the wooden plate did.
The wooden plate gained more heat from Kumar's hand than the metal plate did.

subject: Science
text:
The diagram shows the fruits and seeds of different plants: X has a wing-like structure, Y has a hair-like structure, Z has a fibrous husk. A second diagram shows a seed germinating (stage 1 seed, stage 2 seedling with seed leaf, stage 3 young plant).
(a) Based only on the observable characteristics, which one is most likely dispersed by water? Explain your answer.

(c) State all the conditions needed for the seed to germinate from stage 1 to stage 2.

answer: (a) Z. It has a fibrous husk that traps air and allows it to float on water.  (b) Fruit Y depends on the availability of wind for dispersal.  (c) Warmth/suitable temperature, oxygen/air and water.  (d) The food in the seed leaf had been used up.

subject: Science
text:

answer: (a) 60 beats per minute  (b) (i) Point B (ii) Point D  (c) His heart rate decreased. His heart pumped blood more slowly / pumped less blood as less oxygen and digested food were needed.

subject: Science
text:
The graph shows the amount of undigested food entering and leaving different parts of the digestive system (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine).
(b) State two functions of the small intestine.

David designed a simple flood warning system: a wooden block with sheet A on top floats on rainwater in a container; two metal rods (held in rubber) hang above sheet A; a bulb and a bell are connected to batteries. Rainwater enters the container through hole H.

answer: (a) It is a conductor of electricity.  (b) They are arranged in parallel, so if either the bulb or the bell fuses, the other will still be able to work.  (c) Water enters hole H when it is raining, making the water level in the container rise. Amirah poured 200 ml of boiling water into two similar glass cups, W and V. Cup W is made of two layers of glass with air trapped between them, while cup V is made of a single layer.

Word list: (A) also, (B) for, (C) had, (D) have, (E) in, (F) is, (G) than, (H) then, (J) they, (K) this, (L) though, (M) whether, (N) will, (P) with, (Q) would. Each word can be used only once.

I never thought I would feel nostalgic about a car park. __(26)__ particular open-air car park was conveniently located at the heart of Holland Village, a buzzing neighbourhood in Singapore which I __(27)__ been visiting since young. The car park was nothing special, but it was always there, __(28)__ I was looking to park my car or take a shortcut to the hawker centre. I thought it __(29)__ always be there – a reliable and constant fixture in the background of every memory I had made in Holland Village over the years. One day, the car park was replaced by a shopping mall. When I visited the shopping mall __(30)__ the first time, I was struck by how modern everything looked – and how sad it made me.

I do not remember exactly when the Holland Village I initially knew started fading away. What I do know __(31)__ we lose places bit by bit as the years go by. First, it was the car park that I was so used to seeing. __(32)__, it was the iconic magazine store that had over 80 years of history in Holland Village. I felt a sense of loss – not only had the bits and pieces of the place disappeared but the feeling of familiarity had __(33)__ faded.

I stopped visiting Holland Village eventually. I did not like how I noticed a new feature every time I visited. I felt as __(34)__ the neighbourhood had betrayed my memory of it by simply keeping up __(35)__ the times. Although the changes in the neighbourhood began before I could recognise it as a loss, the memories I had with it will stay with me forever.
